angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 6,235,559 km at 134.84 pc = 0.62 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Hunt & Reffert (2023), Improving the open cluster census. II. An all-sky cluster catalogue with Gaia DR3, A&A 673, A114; CDS J/A+A/673/A114, Table 3 (clusters), Melotte_22: dist50 134.84134308 pc, the distance of the Pleiades, of which Merope is a member; its own parallax (McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson 2017 adopt 116.55 pc from Gaia DR1 or the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007) is less certain than the cluster's depth (half its members within 2.70 pc of the centre), and the Hipparcos-era parallaxes of the bright Pleiades are the ones the cluster's distance controversy showed biased (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202346285): 134.84134308 +/- 2.7 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 7.0670 +/- 0.2862 mas (same row, RUWE 2.33), 24.7 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 8.963 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17608: radius 7.747 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 211.434 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.783) and temperature; scaled from the paper's distance, 116.55 pc, to the cluster's, 134.84 pc: at a fixed temperature the radius grows with the distance, so 7.747 x 134.84/116.55 = 8.963 solar radii (luminosity 283.0) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 6,235,559 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 7913 +/- 3358 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17608: effective temperature 7913 +/- 3358 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.448) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17608: effective temperature 7913 +/- 3358 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.448) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
surfaceGravitySource: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.92 from 2001A&A...378..861C; the 2 published values span log g 2.92 to 4, across which the limb law changes by at most 2.6% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2001A%26A...378..861C)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 215) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
